name: English
learnerProfile: reads and understands everyday English at about IELTS 4.0-5.0; reads at roughly a young child's level. NOT an absolute beginner. Content must be worth their time and build reading confidence.
styleGuidance: Natural, everyday English. Prefer short, plain words and active voice over long sentences. Use contractions. Only use formal or academic register at levels 5-6.
pronunciationGuidance: Sound rules English learners commonly miss: word stress (the stressed syllable changes the whole word), schwa reduction in unstressed syllables, silent letters in common words (know, hour, answer), the voiced/unvoiced distinction between /v/ and /w/, and word-initial consonant clusters in words like 'three' and 'street'. Explain in the learner's own language; do not use a phonetic scheme the learner has not been taught.
exampleGuidance: Keep examples short — under about 10 words, or 2 short clauses.

1.grammar: Present simple and present continuous, basic articles and prepositions, everyday nouns and verbs

2.grammar: Past simple and present perfect, comparatives, common connectors (but, because, so)

3.grammar: Past continuous vs past perfect, relative clauses (who, which, that), modals of obligation

4.grammar: Reported speech, passive voice, conditionals (first and second)

5.grammar: Abstract topics, formal and journalistic register, hedging and concession

6.grammar: Idioms, academic writing conventions, nuanced connectors
